verdict.rationale: Tailscale documents a mesh overlay network that connects devices to servers without port forwarding or public IPs, and community reports confirm SSH-from-anywhere access. However, it is itself a WireGuard-based overlay VPN, and hands-on evidence says NAT traversal sometimes falls back to DERP relays, so connections are not guaranteed to be relay-free. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of direct peer-to-peer connection behavior, any guarantee of no relay fallback, and operation without a VPN overlay.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can connect directly to my servers without relying on a cloud relay, proxy, or VPN

citations.quote: Across clouds or on-prem, Tailscale’s mesh overlay network connects it all.
Connect devices on your private tailnet without port forwarding or public IPs.
MagicDNS hostnames let them browse http://laptop:8000 or SSH from anywhere.
